text:
mike: quick PSA — after the runtime patch last night p99 host-side overhead up ~3.2ms. preparse CPU spike ~18%. seeing more smallwrite syscalls.
anya: ugh. do you have any flamegraphs or traces?
mike: uploaded a trace to the perf bucket: s3://perf/redwood/4949990000/host-preparse-flame.svg and a short snippet:
```
preparse  | cpu 18% | parse_lines + memcpy 4.1ms | writev 1.2ms
grpc-send | writev calls 6 -> 12 per request
```
ryan: first thought — kernel selection path might be toggling the mini-batch hint. that can cause extra buffer copies when we fall back to smallwrite path.
ben: also check kv-cache miss rate. if parse is slower it can push more KV lookups off critical path and increase misses -> extra back-and-forth.
lisa: noticed this morning some TLS connections show repeated gRPC write fragmentation. HPACK inflate on headers makes writev smaller which increases syscall overhead :facepalm:
deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-20T02:14:01Z by @mike rolled runtime:v3.7.4 — feature: adaptive-kernel-hint
anya: can we toggle adaptive-kernel-hint off for a canary? mike, can you flip the flag for Canary pool A and gather p50/p95/p99?
mike: yeah flipping now for pool-a. will run a quick smoke and post numbers in ~20m.
ryan: also queue up a microbench: 1) disable mini-batch hint, 2) force smallwrite->coalesce path, 3) baseline. compare syscall counts + memcpy bytes.
ben: I'll add a tiny KV hit/miss tracer to the canary to see if parse slowdown correlates with kv thrash.
lisa: add a socket coalescing metric too (we have a toggle in host-proxy: socket.writev_coalesce=true/false). helps prove whether writev fragmentation is root cause.
mike: plan: 1) canary flag off, 2) collect traces, 3) kernel/hint telemetry + kv tracer + coalesce flag matrix. posting results in this thread.
anya: thanks — if p99 drops back <1ms we should revert the adaptive hint until we get a kernel-level fix. :thumbsup:
ryan: i'll run the microbench now and push results inline.
mike: thx everyone. ping if you see regressions in dedicated clusters. will update at 4949990024 when metrics land.
